A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their text, equations, four figures, and Appendices A–D support reliable comparison, including matching content across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original linear-attention simulations, TabPFN experiments on T4, and GPT-2 adaptation experiments in Figures 1–3 and Section 6. Appendix D redisplays the TabPFN results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original simulations and TabPFN and GPT-2 experiments, including the results in Appendix D.

M1.justification: The linear-attention architecture, squared-loss objective, fixed context/query split, and single-step rank-one update in Proposition 3.1 remain unchanged. The statement that GPT-2 adaptation updates all parameters adds implementation disclosure without establishing a changed method.

E1.justification: Both evaluate Gaussian linear tasks, covariance-shift scenarios, and T4 tabular classification using TabPFN v2. The expanded T4 description explains preparation of the existing benchmark, including conversion of regression datasets, without reporting additional task evaluations.

E2.justification: The comparator sets remain unchanged: TabPFN with versus without TTT, pretrained versus zero-initialized linear models, and pretrained versus randomly initialized GPT-2. Newly cited methods are not added to the experimental comparisons.

E3.justification: The reported sample-size sweeps, covariance settings, metrics, and TabPFN training budget of 50 iterations per group are retained. The new split and preprocessing information documents previously unspecified settings rather than revising a stated protocol.

E4.justification: The context-length, initialization, covariance-alignment, and multiple-gradient-step analyses remain unchanged. Figure 2c retains the same step-size-decay comparison, and Appendix D retains the same logarithmic-axis display. Added explanatory prose does not introduce another analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report averaging the GPT-2 experiment over three runs with different random seeds. No repeated-run counts, uncertainty-reporting practices, confidence intervals, or significance tests are added or revised.

E6.justification: Figures 1–4 retain the same plotted results and comparisons. The newly stated TabPFN accuracy increase from approximately 0.2 to 0.45 describes points already displayed in v1. The approximately fivefold context reduction and initialization crossover findings are also retained.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, assumptions, theorem statements, and proofs are retained after matching numbering. v1's approximation-error discussion in Remark B.4 moves to Remark 4.3 in v2 with equivalent reasoning; it is not a new bound or proof.

C1.justification: The central claims about single-step TTT, distribution shift, initialization regimes, and reduced TabPFN context requirements remain unchanged. The added emphasis on one-step computational efficiency restates claims already made in v1's Section 6.1 and Discussion.

C2.justification: Section 4 adds an explanation of non-monotonic loss through competing initial-loss and rank-one-adaptation effects. Section 6.2 adds an interpretation of the near-zero-shot TabPFN gains through task memorization. These refine interpretation without changing the underlying evidence or applicability boundaries.

D1.justification: Section 6.2 newly specifies the minimum 1,250 samples, 80/20 split, selection of up to 10 frequent classes, 100 randomly selected features, and quantile-based conversion of regression tasks to classification. Section 6.3 clarifies that GPT-2 adaptation updates all parameters. These improve documentation of retained experiments.

R1.justification: v2 adds Thomas et al. (2024), Hardt and Sun (2024), Hübotter et al. (2025), and Li et al. (2025), modestly extending discussion of tabular fine-tuning, language-model TTT, and linear attention. The publication update for Li et al. (2024) refers to an existing cited work.

P1.justification: v2 expands selected explanations and experimental descriptions, lightly revises the introduction and discussion, and moves the approximation-error remark into the main text. The section organization and most prose remain intact; citation style and title capitalization also change.

P2.justification: The figures retain their plotted content, with limited caption refinements such as identifying TabPFN v2. Figure placement changes, including Figure 4 moving onto a separate page. The title becomes bold and affiliation logos are added, while the overall layout remains similar.

improvement.justification: v2 fills specific documentation gaps in Sections 6.2–6.3 and adds a useful explanation of non-monotonic loss in Section 4. These changes improve reproducibility and interpretation of the existing work. The theoretical results and experimental evidence remain unchanged, making the overall quality gain limited.
